scenes.heading: DNA structure
scenes.sub: How one molecule stores and copies life's instructions
scenes.say: DNA carries the instructions for every living thing, from bacteria to blue whales. Its shape explains how it stores information safely and copies itself accurately every time a cell divides.

scenes.heading: Nucleotides
points: DNA is a polymer of nucleotides
And one of four bases: A, T, G or C
The order of bases carries the information
scenes.say: DNA is a polymer, a long chain of repeating units called nucleotides. Each nucleotide has a phosphate, a deoxyribose sugar and one of four bases: A, T, G or C. Only the base changes, so the information is in the order of the bases.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: A rope ladder twisted into a spiral
scenes.science: A double helix: sugar–phosphate sides, base-pair rungs
scenes.breaks: each DNA rung is really two bases meeting in the middle, and the two strands run in opposite directions (antiparallel).
scenes.say: Picture a rope ladder, twisted into a spiral. The side ropes are the sugar–phosphate backbones, held by strong bonds. The rungs are pairs of bases, held in the middle by weak hydrogen bonds. Twist it, and you get a double helix.

scenes.heading: Complementary base pairing
points: A always pairs with T: 2 hydrogen bonds
G always pairs with C: 3 hydrogen bonds
Apples in the Tree, Car in the Garage
scenes.say: Bases pair like a charger that only fits one port. A always pairs with T, using two hydrogen bonds. G always pairs with C, using three. Remember: Apples in the Tree, Car in the Garage. The two strands are complementary, not identical.

scenes.heading: Chargaff's rule
scenes.question: Double-stranded DNA contains 30% adenine. What percentage is guanine?
lines: A pairs with T, so T = 30%
scenes.say: Because every A has a T partner, the amounts of A and T are equal, and so are G and C. If A is thirty percent, T is thirty percent too. That leaves forty percent for G and C, so guanine is twenty percent.
scenes.caption: Because every A has a T partner, the amounts of A and T are equal, and so are G and C. If A is 30%, T is 30% too. That leaves 40% for G and C, so guanine is 20%.

scenes.heading: DNA replication
steps: Free nucleotides pair up: A–T, G–C
DNA polymerase joins and checks them
scenes.say: To copy DNA, helicase unzips the double helix by breaking the hydrogen bonds. Each strand becomes a template. Free nucleotides pair with the exposed bases, and DNA polymerase joins them into a new backbone and checks for mistakes.

scenes.heading: Semi-conservative
points: Each new molecule: one old + one new strand
Like a jacket unzipped, each half rebuilt
scenes.say: Each new DNA molecule keeps one old strand and one new strand. That's called semi-conservative replication. If a wrong base slips in and isn't fixed, the sequence changes permanently. That's a mutation.

points: Double helix of two antiparallel strands
A with T, G with C
scenes.say: Quick recap. DNA is made of nucleotides twisted into a double helix. A pairs with T, and G with C. Helicase unzips, DNA polymerase builds, and each copy keeps one old strand. Now try the practice questions!
